terms.grammar: adjective (participle of sinō), with esse and a phrase of place
evidence: Liv. 30.24.9: in quō (sinū) sita Carthāgō est (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Verr. 2.4.106: locus in mediā īnsulā situs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of towns, buildings, rooms and things set somewhere. Of a person it means “laid to rest, buried” (hīc situs est, Cic. Leg. 2.57), and with in and the ablative “resting with, depending on” (in vōbīs sita est, Cic. Mur. 83) (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Lewis & Short s.v. appōnō: “placed or situated near”

phrases.latin: Trīclīnium situm est inter culīnam et balneum.
phrases.english: The dining room is between the kitchen and the bathroom.
The city lies at the bend of the river.

sources: Lewis & Short: situs
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 120, 341. Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are copied from its citations (s.v. sinō).
Lewis & Short: jaceo
